title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Departures Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Departures Board
options.lineage: Solari split-flap boards in rail and airport concourses
options.thesis: Every project is a departure: shipped ones have left, and the board never lies about which.
options.viewport: A full-width departures board as the hero: ERIN NODLAND clacks in flap by flap, then seven project rows resolve with DEPARTED / BOARDING / DELAYED, on a flat enamel-blue concourse sign.
options.risk: Tips into theme-park kitsch if the flap mechanics are faked or the signage type is set timidly.

raised.raise: Every departure row is its own deep link, and back returns you to the exact board position.
Status is the board's own printed text in its own columns; no pills, badges or chrome.
One orchestrated flip timeline drives the whole board, replayable with a Refresh board control and stilled under reduced motion.
Open a departure and you follow one journey end to end: its route strip shows the pipeline as stations.
Flat, unmodulated enamel colour committed at page scale; no gradients, glow or glass anywhere.
Each project owns one line colour that carries from its board row into its route strip, read before any word.

options.label: Workflow Canvas
options.thesis: The portfolio is a live workflow: projects are nodes, and data visibly runs between them.
options.viewport: A pannable canvas with a trigger node named Erin feeding into seven project nodes, one executing live.
options.risk: The most literal reading of the subject; it risks looking like a screenshot of the tool rather than a site.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The portfolio as one continuous typed transcript on glass.
options.viewport: An 80-column transcript that prints each project as a session.
options.case: Fuses cleanly but is the category default you already rejected as too AI.
options.kept: System states print themselves rather than appearing as chrome.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from every AI developer portfolio.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Each project is a one-bit card you flip through with painted buttons.
options.viewport: A single fixed card with bitmap menus and a stack of project cards behind it.
options.case: Hiring managers do not identify with it, and one-bit screenshots bury the proof.
options.kept: Every card is addressable, and back retraces your trail.
options.risk: Reads as nostalgia for a tool the audience never used.

options.label: Paper Automata
options.thesis: Turn a crank and each project performs as a paper figure.
options.viewport: A procession of paper figures along one crank line.
options.case: Charming but hides what the systems do behind metaphor.
options.kept: One shared timeline drives all motion, with pause and reverse.

options.label: Rain-Night City
options.thesis: Projects as lit buildings and transit lines across a night skyline.
options.viewport: A skyline band with amber transit stitching project towers together.
options.case: Atmospheric, but the mood competes with the evidence.
options.kept: Following one light journey end to end.
options.risk: Pretty wallpaper with the work pushed to the margins.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: Each project is a swelling lobe of flat colour on a cream coast.
options.viewport: One green lobe fills the viewport with a yellow GATE capsule.
options.case: Joyful, but hiring managers read it as a leisure brand, not engineering.
options.kept: Flat, unmodulated colour committed at page scale.

options.label: Endurance Livery
options.thesis: Stripes and number roundels as an identity system for each project.
options.viewport: A stripe spine running nose to tail with a lit roundel per project.
options.case: Speed reads well, but racing borrows credibility the work already has.
options.kept: An identity that reads before any word, carried across every surface.
options.risk: Costume, not substance, for this audience.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The polished developer portfolio: name, one-line pitch, project cards, contact.
canonCard.viewport: Name and pitch left, a sticky nav, a card grid of projects with screenshots.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the other candidates by design.
